evaluation_rows: in-scope routine total-chlorine samples (v1 cleaning rules) with sampled_at after the cutoff

models.known_site: E6 = average(B6 regression kriging with site effects, G6 gradient boosting)
models.unseen_site: E7 = average(B7 regression kriging, G7 gradient boosting); no site history. G7 uses same-week same-region neighbor contrasts, which need the target's utility sampling-region code (removing them changes development RMSE by 0.000: modeling/sensitivity.py). Refit per fold with the frozen specification in the unseen-site protocol.

metrics: RMSE (95% cluster-bootstrap CI over places) and paired RMSE difference vs. the comparator
coverage, width and interval score of 80% intervals (C0 and C2)
AUC and recall for samples < 2.5 mg/L
hypotheses: H1 (known sites): E6 has lower RMSE than B5p, the strongest Step 2 reference on the most recent data (2024-26; a deliberately hard bar); supported if the 95% cluster-bootstrap CI of the RMSE difference lies below 0.
H2 (unseen sites): E7 has lower RMSE than B4p, likewise the strongest reference on 2024-26; same criterion.
H3 (calibration): the primary 80% intervals (known: C0, unseen: C2) cover between 75% and 85% of post-cutoff samples in each protocol.
H4 (outages, only if Kubala-outage samples exist after the cutoff): C2 coverage during outages is closer to 80% than C0 coverage.
when: once, on the first export with at least 12 months of samples after the cutoff
command: uv run python -m chlorine.modeling.prospective evaluate --raw NEW.xlsx --confirm

amendments.change: H1/H2 wording: the comparators B5p/B4p are the strongest references on 2024-26 (not the best on 2023 validation, which were B5/B4). Comparators, models, metrics and criteria unchanged; no post-cutoff data exists or was viewed.

(1) E7 description corrected: it uses no site history but is not strictly public-data-only (G7's same-region neighbor contrast needs the utility region code); a strict-public variant E7s is equivalent on development data (pooled 2017-2023 RMSE difference 0.000). (2) The model-code fingerprint now covers the import closure of the frozen models instead of whole folders, so unrelated new modules (modeling/sensitivity.py) do not invalidate it. Models are unchanged: a refit reproduces both registered model fingerprints. No post-cutoff data exists or was viewed.

code_fingerprint_definition: model = import closure of modeling/prospective.py excluding cleaning/ (AST without docstrings)
